newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Dull market to keep SE Asian prices soft.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Dull market to keep SE Asian prices soft.

text.p: The Southeast Asian rubber market is probably in for another dull week as flat demand is expected to put a dampener on prices, traders said on Monday.
"I think we're in for another dull week with a downward bias on prices," the chief rubber dealer at one trade house said.
"Until buyers start coming back, the market should stay flat," one Malaysian trader said. "So far, there's no sign of any fresh buying."
Traders said that while prices could be supported by technical factors, the absence of any export business has kept the market in the doldrums since December.

Most buyers from Europe and the U.S. have already bought their rubber requirements until the first quarter of this year. "It seems that both buyers and traders are taking a wait-and-see position. This is an unfavourable situation because we don't know where the market is going to go," said one trader in Indonesia.
"Everybody is looking for buyers. It's so quiet, it's terrible," a trader for a Singapore-based brokerage house added.
Some interest may come in from China over the short-term, but the steep prices producers are asking may curb any buying.
"There have been some inquiries from China but the asking price was a bit high," said one trader in Kuala Lumpur.
Traders said the current wintering period, when rubber trees shed their leaves and latex flow slows, has not limited supplies since there are ample stocks available in the market.
"The wintering has already been well-discounted at the moment," a dealer in Singapore said.
Another trader in the city-state said: "No one is paying any attention to wintering anymore."

"In theory, wintering will lead to tight supply and then firmer prices. But what is happening now is that prices are remaining low," another trader in Indonesia said, adding ample stocks meant buyers did not need to make fresh purchases.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark RSS1 on Friday at 302 Malaysian cents a kg for March buyer, down a cent from the previous week. Drum latex was offered by trading houses unchanged at 237 cents a kg.
In Indonesia, the March SIR20 was seen unchanged at 53.50 U.S. cents/lb FOB Medan and Surabaya, at 53.25 FOB Palembang and at 53.00 FOB Pontianak and Jambi.

In Thailand, thin demand and a softer tone to the market in Japan dragged prices down last week, traders said. While there were active inquiries from China and Japan, the actual level of trading remained modest.
"Rubber moved in a narrow range all week with an upward bias, but the price was still low compared to last week. The market was pretty dull," a dealer in Hat Yai said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for April shipment fell to 121-122 US cents a kg from 123 US cents last week. Latex was steady at 93 cent a kg.
